package_info.package_name: Blender Photo Editor-Easy Photo Background Editor
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions available at time of report)
package_info.why_malicious: The app embeds malicious code that intercepts users’ Facebook credentials and exfiltrates them to an attacker-controlled server. The stolen credentials are then used to access the victim’s Facebook account and payment information, enabling the attacker to run unauthorized ad campaigns and commit financial fraud. This constitutes both credential theft and abuse of user financial resources, making the entire package malicious.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user attempts Facebook login via app interface)
execution_context.file_location: Android app code, likely within a custom Facebook login Activity or background service (e.g., com.blenderphotoeditor.auth.CustomFacebookLogin.java)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code captures Facebook login credentials entered by the user into a custom login form, transmits the credentials via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled external domain, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code directly accesses user-supplied Facebook credentials and sends them to a non-Facebook domain, which is a clear indicator of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate photo editor app should never request or handle Facebook credentials directly, nor transmit them to any server other than Facebook’s official authentication endpoints via the official SDK.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may use Facebook login through the official SDK, which never exposes raw credentials to the app or transmits them to third-party servers.
key_indicators: Custom Facebook login form implementation instead of using official SDK
Direct access to user-entered email and password fields
Hardcoded external URL for credential exfiltration
HTTP POST requests containing credential data to non-Facebook domains

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after successful credential theft and token acquisition)
execution_context.file_location: Android app code, likely in a background service or ad management module (e.g., com.blenderphotoeditor.ads.FraudulentAdManager.java)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after obtaining the victim’s Facebook session token, the code uses the stolen token to interact with Facebook’s ad management APIs, creating and running ad campaigns that charge the victim’s payment method without their consent.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code leverages stolen Facebook tokens to programmatically create ad campaigns, resulting in unauthorized financial transactions and account abuse.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A photo editor app should not interact with Facebook’s ad management APIs or access user payment information for any purpose, especially without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Only official Facebook ad management tools or apps with explicit user authorization should create ad campaigns, and never using credentials or tokens obtained without user knowledge.
key_indicators: Use of Facebook API calls with tokens not obtained via official SDK
Automated creation of ad campaigns without user interaction
Access to or use of payment information linked to Facebook account
Background service activity related to Facebook ad management in a non-advertising app

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious app and is prompted to log in with Facebook credentials via a custom login form.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credentials are intercepted and exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server.

attack_chain.action: Stolen credentials are used to obtain a valid Facebook session token and access the victim’s Facebook account and associated payment information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker creates and runs unauthorized ad campaigns, incurring charges to the victim’s payment method.

behavioral_signatures: Android apps implementing custom Facebook login forms that request credentials directly from users
Transmission of Facebook login credentials to external, non-Facebook domains during authentication
Background creation of Facebook ad campaigns using session tokens not obtained via official SDK flows
Access to Facebook ad management APIs by non-advertising or photo editing apps
file_indicators: App code containing hardcoded external URLs or domains for credential exfiltration (e.g., 'https://malicious-domain.com/steal')
Presence of custom Facebook login Activity or class (e.g., CustomFacebookLogin.java) instead of using official Facebook SDK components
References to Facebook ad management API endpoints or classes (e.g., AdManager) in apps not intended for advertising
network_indicators: HTTP or HTTPS POST requests containing Facebook credential data sent to domains not associated with Facebook (e.g., 'malicious-domain.com')
Unusual API calls to Facebook ad endpoints (e.g., /act_{ad_account_id}/campaigns) from apps that are not official ad management tools
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Android apps for custom implementations of Facebook login that request credentials directly and transmit them to non-Facebook domains. Flag apps that make outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing credential data to unknown or suspicious domains during authentication. Analyze app code for hardcoded exfiltration URLs, custom login forms, and references to Facebook ad management APIs in non-advertising apps. Correlate network activity with app behavior to identify unauthorized ad campaign creation using stolen tokens.
